questions.question: For the survey of 40 learners (22 soccer, 15 chess, 9 both), describe how to fill the Venn diagram and give all four region counts with the check.
questions.expected_answer: Fill the overlap first with 9, because each sport's total includes the both-players. Then soccer-only = 22 − 9 = 13, chess-only = 15 − 9 = 6, and neither = 40 − (13 + 9 + 6) = 12. Check: 13 + 9 + 6 + 12 = 40, so every learner is placed exactly once.

questions.question: State the addition rule, explain why the subtraction is needed, and use the rule to find P(soccer or chess) for the survey.
questions.expected_answer: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A and B). Adding the two whole events counts the overlap twice — both-players appear in each event's total — so the overlap is subtracted once. P(soccer or chess) = 22/40 + 15/40 − 9/40 = 28/40 = 7/10, confirmed by the regions 13 + 9 + 6 = 28 out of 40.

questions.question: Explain the difference between mutually exclusive and complementary events, with a die example of events that are exclusive but not complementary.
questions.expected_answer: Mutually exclusive events share no outcomes — they cannot both happen — so P(A and B) = 0 and P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B). Complementary events are mutually exclusive AND exhaustive: together they cover the whole sample space, so their probabilities total 1. 'Less than 3' and 'at least 5' on a die are exclusive (no shared outcome) but not complementary, because the outcomes 3 and 4 belong to neither event.
